desk.headline: Sales up 18% to $6.75bn and adjusted EPS $3.26 beats $2.77 estimate; full-year profit outlook raised on the call
results: Net sales rose 17.7% to $6.75bn, led by data storage and servers, notebooks and software.
Every customer group grew: Commercial +20.8%, UK and Canada +26.0%, Government +9.9%, Education +7.5%.
Gross margin slipped to 20.5% from 21.9% as lower-margin hardware made up more of sales.
Adjusted EPS rose 20% to $3.26; GAAP EPS rose 12% to $2.46.
The quarterly dividend was raised about 8% to $0.68 a share; about $1.03bn is left under the buyback plan.

guidance.summary: The press release has no outlook. On the call CDW lifted its 2026 targets: gross profit growth now mid-to-high single digits (was mid-single) and adjusted EPS growth low double digits (was high single digits).

points: Management named AI-ready infrastructure and data-centre upgrades as the main demand drivers; server and storage sales more than doubled.
The CFO said that growth came mostly from more units sold, not higher prices; notebook prices rose with richer specifications.
AI hardware carries lower margins, so gross margin for 2026 is still expected to be below 2025.
CDW bought data and AI services firm Lovelytics for $525m and issued $1.5bn of bonds, partly to repay $1bn due in December.
About $892m has been returned to shareholders so far this year; net leverage is 2.5 times, inside the 2–3 times target.
